description: Discover how processes share CPU time by taking turns with a fixed time quantum.

discovery.title: CPU Time Is Shared
discovery.summary: Round Robin gives each process a limited time quantum, then rotates unfinished processes back into the ready queue.

sections.title: What is Round Robin?
sections.content: Round Robin is a CPU scheduling method where ready processes take turns using the CPU.

sections.title: Time quantum
sections.content: A time quantum is the maximum amount of CPU time a process receives in one turn.

sections.title: Why processes take turns
sections.content: Taking turns stops one long process from keeping every other ready process waiting for too long.

sections.title: When a process is unfinished
sections.content: If a process still has work after its time quantum, it goes to the back of the ready queue.

sections.title: When a process finishes
sections.content: A process that uses all of its remaining time leaves the CPU and moves to Completed.

sections.title: Time-sharing systems
sections.content: Round Robin is useful when many users or programs should get regular chances to run.

sections.title: FCFS and Round Robin
sections.content: FCFS runs the first process until it finishes. Round Robin pauses unfinished processes after a time quantum so others can run.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of sharing one controller
alternate_explanations.content: Round Robin is like several people sharing one game controller for short turns. Everyone gets a turn before the first person gets the controller again.

alternate_explanations.title: Rotate with quantum 2
alternate_explanations.content: P1 starts with 5 units and uses 2, leaving 3. It moves behind P2 and P3. P2 then uses 2 and returns with 1, so the queue keeps rotating.

introduction.title: Meet Round Robin
introduction.content: Round Robin shares one CPU by giving each waiting process a short turn instead of letting the first one keep the CPU until it finishes.
points: A time quantum is the maximum length of one CPU turn.
An unfinished process returns to the back of Ready Queue.
You will watch the queue rotate so each process gets a chance.

worked_example.title: Watch one turn rotate
worked_example.content: The time quantum is 2 units, so P1 cannot use more than 2 units in one turn.

steps.explanation: P1 begins at the front of the ready queue.
P1 uses two units and still has three units of work left.
Because P1 is unfinished, it goes to the back and P2 gets the next turn.

worked_example.conclusion: Short turns let several processes share the CPU fairly.

next.title: Rotate the ready queue.

action_explanations.run-first-process: P1 leaves the front of Ready Queue and receives the first CPU turn.
action_explanations.use-time-quantum: P1 can use only two units this turn, so it still has work remaining.
action_explanations.return-to-ready-queue: P1 is unfinished, so it returns to the back and makes room for P2.
action_explanations.run-next-process: P2 now gets a turn because it moved to the front while P1 returned to the back.
action_explanations.continue-rotating: Each turn either completes a process or sends it to the back, keeping the queue rotating.
action_explanations.complete-all: Every process has used enough turns to finish, so the completed list contains them all.
